flashcard_questions.q: What does the policy of appeasement mean?
flashcard_questions.a: Giving in to an aggressor's demands to avoid conflict

flashcard_questions.q: Which British Prime Minister made appeasement official policy from 1937?
How many soldiers had Britain and France lost between them in the First World War?
What name is given to the union of Germany and Austria in March 1938?
On what date did German troops march into Austria?
What share of the vote did the rigged Austrian plebiscite of April 1938 claim?
Which leader stopped Hitler's first attempt at union with Austria in 1934?
About how many ethnic Germans lived in the Sudetenland?
Which huge arms factory lay inside the Sudetenland?
Who led the Sudeten German Party?
On what date was the Munich Agreement signed?
What phrase did Chamberlain use on returning to Britain from Munich?
What share of its land did Czechoslovakia lose under the Munich Agreement?
In which month did Hitler take over the rest of Czechoslovakia, breaking his Munich promise?
Which 1940 book blamed Chamberlain and the other appeasers for the war?

notes: 15 cards: 5 event to date, 4 statistic, 3 term-or-agreement to name, 2 person, 1 quotation. Split the six reasons for appeasement rather than listing them, so only the WWI casualty figure survives as a card; the rest is causal essay material.
